title: The completed trivial-character Fourier line is the common-stage unit
statement: Let F be a Fourier setting [def-fourier-set]: finite-field characteristic p, coefficient prime l different from p, a chosen algebraic closure Omega of Q_l and a finite coefficient stage containing the pth roots of unity. Let X be a Noetherian scheme of characteristic p on global functions, with l invertible in every residue field. Form the degree-zero completed Artin--Schreier object for the trivial prime-field character and zero function by [def-fd-adic-fourier-realization], rationalize at the Fourier coefficient stage and regard it as an actual common-stage pair [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. This pair is isomorphic to the specified common-stage coefficient unit of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. No shift, geometric pullback, tensor functor or Weil structure is asserted here.

proof.text: The integral lift of the trivial character is trivial: the coefficient embedding is injective and its values are prescribed by fourierIntegralCharacter_existsUnique. The prime-field realization is artinSchreierSheafOf over the lifted prime field. Apply the existing trivial-character isomorphism nonempty_iso_artinSchreierSheafOf_one from [lem-fd-as-characters]; it identifies the invariant summand with constant regular sections.

Comparison inverse image and the fixed-ring/constant-ring module equivalence take this regular sheaf to the constant regular pro-etale module. Completed scalar extension takes it to the completed ring acting on itself: multiplication is the forward map and m mapped to 1 tensor m is the inverse, with the scalar balancing relation giving both inverse identities. Apply the degree-zero single functor. The quotient projections give exactly the coherent ring-unit system. The reduction/limit adjunction and completeness identify the completed regular module with the prescribed reconstructed integral unit of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso].

Rationalize the integral isomorphism at the Fourier coefficient stage. The least finite coefficient field lies in that stage. The common-unit scalar comparison pullbackTensorCommonUnitStage identifies the transition of the least-stage unit with the unit there; compose with the pair-category isomorphism to a larger stage, in the appropriate direction. This yields the displayed common-stage isomorphism and also applies to the empty scheme.

theorem fourierTrivialCharacter_unit (F : FourierSetting.{u}) (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsNoetherian X] [CharP Γ(X, ⊤) F.field.p]
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (F.coefficients.l : X.residueField x)] :
    Nonempty ((⟨fourierCoefficientStage F,
      (sfRationalConstructibleLocalization F.coefficients.l (fourierCoefficient F) X).obj
        ⟨fourierAdicArtinSchreier F X 1 0, fourierAdicArtinSchreier_mem F X 1 0⟩⟩ :
          generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory F.coefficients.l F.coefficients.Qbar X)
      ≅ pullbackTensorCommonUnit F.coefficients.l F.coefficients.Qbar X)
